Native terrain and selected-look caption productions
===================================================

Scope and source meaning
------------------------
These notes describe offline disassembly of BOTH Windows PE images configured
in data/runtime/native-pe-images.json. Addresses below are RVAs, not live VAs.
native-owners.tsv records each image identity and actual code/table boundary.
The corresponding reference-*.asm and classic-*.asm retain the instruction
streams. native-branches.tsv retains every jcc/jmp, including empty/default
edges; native-switches.tsv contains actual dword destinations and byte remaps,
not merely addresses of indirect JMP instructions.

This is a finite inventory of the caption producers and their source fields.
It is not an enumeration of every possible world-specific output sentence.
RAW material/plant/body-part text and procedural names remain dynamic inputs.
Existing RAW/name translation catalogs supply those domains; their strings
must not be replaced by a guessed finite list. Calls into generic item, unit,
building and generated-name formatters are recorded, not recursively claimed
to have been decompiled in this terrain extraction.

The original tile-hover-sources.tsv catalog retained reference-image LEA
operands. This extraction additionally retains printable operands of any
RIP-relative instruction, including SIMD loads, plus printable MOVABS bytes.
Suffixes such as "ages" loaded into another portion of a local string are
source operands, not separate displayed productions.

Fortress cached terrain source and both actual draw branches
-----------------------------------------------------------
The user explicitly identifies the supplied screenshot as FORTRESS mode.
Its gold frame is not evidence for an Adventure consumer. The exact frame
instance and the precise runtime masking cause have not been observed.
The native Fortress ownership below is established by PE code and RTTI.

Reference RTTI: viewscreen_dwarfmodest vtable slots2/3 at0x16be510/16be518
point to input0x8b3170 and render wrapper0x8bcc70. Their actual MSVC locator
is0x17a1fb0; type descriptor0x18c9568 names.?AVviewscreen_dwarfmodest@@.
Classic slots0x16b9400/16b9408 point to0x8b09f0/0x8ba4f0; locator0x179c8c0,
type descriptor0x18c3538 carries the same class name. These exact slot/locator
records are saved in native-terrain-consumer-ownership.tsv. A missing direct
slot reference is recorded as such, without guessing a class name.

Reference render wrapper0x8bcc70 calls main renderer0x3d6950 at0x8bccc6;
Classic wrapper0x8ba4f0 calls0x3d4510 at0x8ba546. Reference Fortress input
refresh call0x8b597f ->0x4085f0; Classic0x8b31ff ->0x4061b0. Input caches
the selected x/y/z at0x18acef8/fa/fc (Classic0x18a6ec8/ca/cc), changes the
cache timestamp, passes the selected coordinate words into the look producer,
or clears the list through0x8bf060 (Classic0x8bc8e0). The renderer at0x3f9303
uses the SAME cached x word and skips an invalid coordinate(-30000).

The producer clears the old pointer vector before processing the requested
tile. Its existing complete body, conditional branches and decoded flow table
are retained in lookinfo-producer.asm. Valid-tile/visibility/memory/sense
branches determine which records are made. Ordinary terrain record allocation
is0x4097c2, sets type1 at0x4097f7, stores coordinates at+0x1c/+0x1e/+0x20,
and calls the cached constructor0x406860 at0x409807. It appends that exact
record pointer at0x40981c or takes the vector growth call0x40982d ->0x420e40.
Classic production sites are reference RVA-0x2440. Each record is0x50 bytes;
its std::string display_str is at+0x28, length+0x38, capacity+0x40, followed
by foreground/background/bold fields+0x48/+0x4a/+0x4c.

The cached constructor clears display_str, dispatches its16-type table, and
type1 entry0x406973 calls terrain0xe7d330 at0x406995 with coordinates from
the same record and growth=true. Classic entry0x404533 calls0xe782a0 at
0x404555. All694 terrain selector routes, defaults/aliases, material and
plant/growth source branches below therefore supply this Fortress field.
"peat Cavern Floor" is one material-noun production, not a unique UI branch.

Fortress main renderer has exactly two cached-list caption loops:
* Reference first frame starts0x3f9356, top=7, bottom=list.size+8,
  right=[rbp+0xb4]-37, left=right-60. Its row is x=left+2,y=8+index.
  Iterator temporaries are rbp+0x268/+0x270;0x3f9543 dereferences the record,
  0x3f9546 adds0x28; addst0x3f9553 (return0x3f9558) consumes that field.
  Classic frame starts0x3f6f16, addst0x3f7113, return0x3f7118.
* Reference second frame starts0x3f9594, top=3, bottom=list.size+5,
  same left/right expression, row x=left+2,y=5+index. Its iterators are
  rbp+0x278/+0x280;0x3f9765 dereferences the record,0x3f9768 adds0x28;
  addst0x3f9775 (return0x3f977a) consumes that field. Classic frame starts
  0x3f7154, addst0x3f7335, return0x3f733a.
Both loops use record color fields directly. Neither copies the terrain
caption into a separate button/widget string. They draw all cached record
types rather than manufacturing a second terrain-only source.

Renderer gate0x3f933c compares byte0x18a75b8 with r15b: equal enters the
second frame; otherwise byte0x18a75bc bit2 must be set for the first frame.
The exact flag names are not inferred from geometry. Empty list, invalid
cached coordinate, disabled gate or exhausted iterator emits no row. The
first loop draws the complete rectangular border through texture global
0x264bd14..0x264bd34; the second uses additional joined-corner textures
0x264bd3c/0x264bd44. A one-record first frame is three cells high. This
explains native geometry without assigning the screenshot to one branch.

All RIP references to cached list/vector fields
-----------------------------------------------
extract_fortress_look_consumers.py reads the whole .text section, considers
every displacement alignment and immediate suffix, then retains only actual
RIP instructions decoded from owning procedures or the four no-pdata leaves.
Every reference to vector.begin/end/capacity(+0/+8/+16) is saved with actual
PC, target field and full owner interval in native-look-vector-references.tsv
and native-look-vector-owners.tsv. Both configured editions have120 actual
references in11 owners each:113 references in7 unwind owners plus7 references
in4 leaves. Raw navigation coincidences are decoded before rejection; the
reference0xc60226 coincidence straddles two unrelated leaf instructions.

Reference owner / Classic owner / operation / number of references:
0x3d6950 /0x3d4510   Fortress renderer, both loops above                 7
0x4085f0 /0x4061b0   coordinate producer/append                         57
0x420e40 /0x41ea00   pointer-vector reallocate/insert                    11
0x7f3cb0 /0x7f1530   Adventure selected-look renderer                   22
0x8bf060 /0x8bc8e0   destroy record string+28,free record,clear vector    5
0xaf1190 /0xaee1d0   Adventure main render helper, two list loops        7
0x15e2420/0x15dcf50  global vector storage destructor                    4
0x420dd0 /0x41e990   no-pdata leaf:size                                 2
0x420df0 /0x41e9b0   no-pdata leaf:end iterator                         1
0x420e00 /0x41e9c0   no-pdata leaf:begin iterator                       1
0x420e10 /0x41e9d0   no-pdata leaf:pointer push or tailcall reallocate  3
The leaves return the vector's size or pointer iterators, or insert pointers;
they do not copy display_str. A consumer can call these leaves without its own
global RIP reference, so this direct global inventory alone does NOT establish
consumer closure. The leaf-call edges are separately extracted below. The
af1190 helper is directly called by the actual
viewscreen_dungeonmodest renderer at0x7f3dba/0x7f3e0c/0x7f3e73, so it is
not assigned to this Fortress screenshot.

Dedicated vector-leaf caller edges
-----------------------------------
native-look-leaf-callers.tsv records every confirmed direct E8 caller to the
four dedicated list leaves in BOTH complete .text sections, with exact call,
return, target, role, owning procedure and owner end. Each byte hit is checked
against the actual decoded CALL from the owner's instruction stream; no-pdata
callers are also decoded if encountered. Source navigation uses overlapping
E8 positions: an E8 immediate/displacement in the preceding instruction must
not swallow the real call. This matters to Classic calls0x3f7275/0x3f7288.

Per edition there are17 actual calls in3 existing vector-reference owners:
Fortress main renderer:3 size +2 begin +2 end =7 calls;
coordinate producer:3 pointer push calls;
Adventure render helper:3 size +2 begin +2 end =7 calls.
Reference Fortress calls:0x3f9317/0x3f936a/0x3f95a8 ->size0x420dd0;
0x3f9487/0x3f96b5 ->begin0x420e00;0x3f949a/0x3f96c8 ->end0x420df0.
Classic Fortress calls:0x3f6ed7/0x3f6f2a/0x3f7168 ->size0x41e990;
0x3f7047/0x3f7275 ->begin0x41e9c0;0x3f705a/0x3f7288 ->end0x41e9b0.
Reference producer calls0x408771/0x408923/0x4089ae ->push0x420e10;
Classic0x406331/0x4064e3/0x40656e ->push0x41e9d0.
Reference Adventure calls0xb02d0a/0xb02e55/0xb03046 ->size,
0xb02f37/0xb03124 ->begin,0xb02f4a/0xb03137 ->end. Classic equivalents
are reference RVA-0x2fc0. Complete caller contexts are retained in both
look-leaf-callers.asm files in addition to already retained full owner bodies.

No leaf caller owner without a direct vector reference exists in these two
images. Accordingly, tracing dedicated leaf calls adds no new list-to-widget
copying owner. This conclusion is based on BOTH actual global-reference and
leaf-call edges, not on global references alone. Arbitrary indirect aliases,
indirect function-pointer consumers or mod code are not claimed absent.
The corrected overlap scan also reran the terrain/constructor/producer
inventory: its original17+22+2 confirmed calls per edition remain unchanged.
The same complete-image navigation/decode also covers direct E9 tail jumps
to terrain and all four dedicated list leaves, including no-pdata owners.
Both images have zero actual E9 edges to these five targets. The resulting
native-terrain-look-tail-edges.tsv has its source-schema header and no rows;
the absence is from actual binary source traversal, not an assumed lack of
tail wrappers. No unresolved no-pdata candidate remains in that traversal.

Direct terrain caller classification and draw-helper ownership
---------------------------------------------------------------
All17 direct terrain calls per edition remain in native-consumers.tsv;
the PE RTTI slot records distinguish Adventure action captions from Fortress
titles rather than classifying by their wording. Eight reference owners have
these actual adventure classes (Classic equivalent in parentheses):
0x83a0e0(0x837960) adventure_environment_pickup_ignite_vegst
0x841440(0x83ecc0) adventure_movement_movest
0x841900(0x83f180) adventure_movement_climbst
0x841bf0(0x83f470) adventure_movement_hold_tilest
0x842050(0x83f8d0) adventure_movement_dismountst
0x8421b0(0x83fa30) adventure_movement_release_hold_tilest
0x8a5540(0x8a2dc0) adventure_movement_shoot_tilest
0x8a64d0(0x8a3d50) adventure_movement_throw_item_at_tilest
Other confirmed calls are the cached constructor above, dungeon selected-look
renderer, two engraving/title-sheet calls in0x14ef90(Classic0x14ef20),
report/announcement assembly in0x8a6e70/0xa398a0/0x15059c0, and direction/
route descriptor helper0x13ea8f0. The announcement consumers append terrain
to a sentence and call0xe3c20 (e.g.0x8a799e/0xa3a0fa/0x15093cd); those
contexts do not supply a new cached Fortress hover record. The sheet calls
use terrain growth=false and have separate existing typed title bindings.

Actual addst0xad9960..0xad9a33 copies the input std::string, optionally
shortens by width, and emits characters through bb190 at0xad9a00. It does
not call addst_flag0xad9870 or top_addst0xad9a40. Flag draw independently
emits through ad8b80 at0xad9920; top draw emits through1bb000 at0xad9ac1.
Classic equivalents: addst0xad69a0..ad6a73 ->bb120 at0xad6a40;
flag0xad68b0..ad699b ->ad5bc0 at0xad6960; top0xad6a80..ad6b3c ->1baf90
at0xad6b01. Full six helper bodies are retained. There is no nested addst
context overwrite in this path.

Runtime integration implication
--------------------------------
The cached terrain production, both Fortress record+28 sources and complete
existing tiles grammar are established. A runtime pass that lets broader
message/title/item masks claim this source before typed Terrain can suppress
an already recognized full terrain sentence; later card restoration can also
replace earlier output. The implemented repair gives proven current native
Terrain sources priority in main and reduced/private/background readers and
preserves an existing complete terrain phrase when card source restoration
runs. This is a concrete reader-order weakness addressed by the code change,
not a claim that the supplied image proves one precise mask execution.

Additional Adventure terrain consumer
--------------------------------------
Reference adventure renderer: 0x7f3cb0..0x7f6aee code; tables through0x7f6c21.
Classic adventure renderer:   0x7f1530..0x7f436e code; tables through0x7f44a1.
The selected-look dispatch reads lookinfost.type at0x7f40e5 and uses table
0x7f6af0 (Classic0x7f4370). Type1 enters0x7f40fe, writes a LOCAL std::string
at rbp-0x30 via terrain call0x7f412a ->0xe7d330 with growth flag TRUE, and
draws that complete field at addst0x7f419e, return0x7f41a3.
Classic: call0x7f19aa ->0xe782a0; addst0x7f1a1e; return0x7f1a23.
The preceding addst0x7f4181 draws the separate " - " separator.

This draw is distinct from the lookinfo cached display_str constructor at
0x406860 and from engraving/title-sheet consumers. A capture limited to
lookinfo.display_str or the sheet title misses this real terrain draw even
when the complete tiles grammar already knows "{material} Cavern Floor".
This additional real consumer had an independent capture omission. It is
retained for complete source coverage and is not the supplied Fortress image.

Selected-look renderer: all13 types
------------------------------------
Type Entry      Complete caption / source operation
0    0x7f41a8   Item id lookup ->item caption formatter0xc65450.
1    0x7f40fe   Terrain compositor0xe7d330, growth=true.
2    0x7f42ba   Unit id lookup ->unit caption formatter0x132e430.
3    0x7f4366   Building id lookup ->virtual caption method[vtbl+0x188].
4    0x7f43f9   Item-backed vermin uses item formatter; otherwise race/caste
                formatter0xaa3bd0 with the quantity branches below.
5    0x7f45c1   Flow type0..13, full subtable described below.
6    0x7f490a   "A Campfire", final draw0x7f498a, return0x7f498f.
7    0x7f51b3   Item-based or matter/extent surface-deposit assembly below;
                final draw0x7f539e, return0x7f53a3.
8    0x7f4240   BuildingItem id ->item formatter, separate " -  " separator.
9    0x7f487b   "A Fire", final draw0x7f48fb, return0x7f4900.
10   0x7f4edd   Water flags +amount, three separate final text pieces below.
11   0x7f506b   Magma flags +amount, three separate final text pieces below.
12   0x7f4999   Track/Spoor assembly +shortening +direction/party suffix.
All Classic entries and draws in this renderer are reference RVA-0x2780.
Types0/1/2/3/4/5/8 use common final draw0x7f419e, return0x7f41a3.
Type outside0..12 jumps0x7f53ad without a caption draw. Missing item/unit/
building lookups also skip this row. Flow out-of-range reaches the shared
draw without assigning a flow caption. These edges do not emit "Unknown".

Vermin quantity: colony flag ->"a colony of "+plural species; count<=1
->singular/caste form; count2..9 ->plural species; count10..49 ->"many "+
plural species; count>=50 ->"a swarm of "+plural species. Item-backed
vermin bypass all those RAW branches through the regular item formatter.

Flow subtable0x7f6b24 (Classic0x7f43a4)
0 Miasma; 1 subtype1 Steam, other subtype Mist; 2 Mist;
3 material state noun; 4 bit15 subterranean Magma Mist, otherwise Lava Mist;
5 Smoke; 6 Dragonfire; 7 Fire; 8 A Web; 9 material state2 noun;
10 material gas-state noun+" Vapor"; 11 An Ocean Wave; 12 Sea Foam;
13 guide-backed item formatter0xa82c10 when guide kind1; null/unsupported/
   empty formatted source falls back to "Item Cloud".
The HUD suffix is capital-V " Vapor". Cached constructor uses " vapor".
Material inputs are flow.subtype, flow.sstype and selected matter state.

Surface deposits
For i_type!=-1: item kind/subtype/material formatter0xa82c10, followed by
native text normalization0x52d650. No quantity-prefix branch is entered.
For i_type==-1: choose prefix from matter_state and extent, then append
material noun0x14d1920 using mat/matg/matstate. Native layout stores these at
lookinfost+0xc/+0x10/+0x14; extent is lookinfost+0x18.
Extent              1                   2                  3
matter_state0       A thin layer of     A small pile of    A pile of
matter_state1       A spattering of     A smear of         A pool of
other matter_state  A dusting of        A small pile of    A pile of
Extent outside1..3 selects no quantity prefix; the material still appends.
The item path and all seven prefix strings are separate real native edges.

Water and magma split draws
Water flags&3 chooses "Stagnant salt water [", "Stagnant water [",
"Salt water [" or "Water [". Prefix calls0x7f4f77/0x7f4fa5/0x7f4fcc/
0x7f4fef, amount call0x7f502e, suffix"/7]" call0x7f5052.
Magma flag&1 chooses "Magma [", otherwise "Lava [". Prefix calls0x7f5137/
0x7f5114, amount call0x7f5176, suffix"/7]" call0x7f519a.
Both amounts come from selected lookinfost+0x8. These are split native
fields, not a complete single std::string passed to one addst caller.

Spoor complete-source and shortening boundary
"Track/Spoor: "+body is composed at rbp-0x10. spoor.type0 adds broken
vegetation; type1 uses creature/caste name, optional material adjective and
body-part RAW name, then print/imprint; type2 uses item caption, optional
material adjective, right/left and print/imprint; type3 unintelligible;
unsupported type adds no body. The0x40 flag chooses print rather than imprint
and enables the substance source lookup0x14d2cc0. Missing substance type
falls back to native type6; optional body-part index/name is range guarded.
No side flag omits right/left; right takes priority when both side flags set.

At0x7f4e21, call0x52dee0 applies a50-character bound BEFORE directions and
"/yours or companion's". Its wrapper checks string.length>limit and only
then tail-jumps0x52d910. The shortening implementation removes leading
A/An/The, then eligible vowels backwards, then resizes if still too long.
Classic wrapper/call/implementation:0x52b900/0x7f26a1/0x52b330.
Only direction-present flag0x2 enters the direction branch; otherwise omit
its suffix. Direction flags are masked&0x1c:0/4/8/12/16/20/24/28 produce
/N,/S,/E,/NE,/W,/NW,/SE,/SW, respectively. Remap encodings not possible
after AND are retained with reachable_mask=0. Party flag optionally appends
"/yours or companion's". Final complete draw0x7f4ed2, return0x7f4ed7.
Translation capture must preserve the pre-shortening source, just as for
the separate cached constructor call0x407ef8 ->0x52d910.

Shared terrain compositor and694-selector main table
----------------------------------------------------
Reference0xe7d330..0xe834fd code; tables through0xe8482c.
Classic0xe782a0..0xe7e46d code; tables through0xe7f79c.
It resets the destination, looks up tile type/coordinates and engraving
quality, dispatches walls BEFORE common terrain, and composes one string.
All reference terrain instruction/table RVAs below shift-0x5090 in Classic.

First wall gate consists of direct arithmetic comparisons plus compressed
tables0xe83500/remap0xe83508 and0xe83578/remap0xe83580. It routes147 enum
values to common wall-family entry0xe82df3. Native-tile-types.tsv records
those effective entries; XML shape/material/special are semantic labels
from data/upstream/df-structures/df.d_basics.xml, not substituted binary data.

Non-wall prefix order: optional Muddy, optional Snow-covered, optional Mossy.
Mud/snow come from block events via0x542e80; moss from0x068010 signed flag.
Then selector=tiletype-1 is bounded0..693 and uses actual compressed table
0xe83678/remap0xe838bc. All694 selectors, aliases and default mappings are
retained. They reach145 different entries, including178 main-table entries
mapped to Unknown before applying the earlier wall gate. Tile0/695/696 and
other values outside the table take Unknown unless intercepted by wall gate.
Unknown is an actual literal at0xe82de7, not an absent dictionary fallback.

The main table factors into these complete source families:
* Tree/parts entry0xe7d6ce: plant lookup; optional generated plant name+", ";
  optional Dead; plant-parts helper or generic Tree fallback; growth list.
* Grass entries0xe7dd5e..0xe7e79f: Sparse/Dense from positive block event
  amount; optional Dry/Dead; plant plural/name if event+RAW found, otherwise
  generic Grass or dead/dry Grass. No event/RAW supplies the generic fallback.
* Flat tracks0xe7e7d2..0xe7f48c: all15 direction strings(N,S,E,W,NS,NE,NW,
  SE,SW,EW,NSE,NSW,NEW,SEW,NSEW); each branches into natural material noun,
  constructed adjective or Ice, then " Track (... )" with native spacing.
  Shoddy prefixes occur before the construction helper where selected.
* Detailed/smooth floor0xe7f48d: engraved quality-marked Detailed+space or
  Smooth, material noun; bit15 optionally appends " Floor".
* Boulder0xe7f6a6: material noun+" Boulder". Driftwood0xe7f736 is literal.
  Pebbles0xe7f74a: material noun+" Pebbles".
* Floor0xe7f7d8: material noun; bit15 optionally appends " Cavern Floor".
  Wet floor0xe7f883 prepends Wet and has the same conditional suffix.
* Sapling0xe7f93f: optional generated name+", ", Dead, then Young plant
  part/name or plant part/name+Sapling; generic Sapling if plant absent.
* Shrub0xe7fa93: optional generated name+", ", Dead, plant part/name and
  growth list; generic Shrub if plant absent.
* Furrowed0xe7ffb8: "Furrowed "+material noun.
* Literal cases0xe80040..0xe80190: Ashes, Waterfall, River Source, Chasm,
  Eerie Glowing Pit, Ice, Glowing Floor, Glowing Barrier, Semi-molten Rock,
  Lava Flow/Magma Flow(bit15), Murky Pool, [Unusable]Murky Pool Slope,
  River, Brook. Underworld Gate and ice/decorated variants are also direct
  stair/floor edges retained in native-literals.tsv and native-tile-types.tsv.
* Stairs0xe801a2..0xe80685: Upward/Downward/Up/Down; grass adjective with
  Sparse/Dense when RAW exists, generic Grassy otherwise; natural material,
  construction/Shoddy, Ice and Underworld Gate branches. Plain direction
  Stairway fallback is a real native edge.
* Upward slope/track0xe80686..0xe81d98: actual slope-usability lookup inserts
  Unusable when false; grassy/dry/dead adjective, material, construction,
  Glacial and plain Upward Slope cases; all15 upward track connections, each
  natural/construction/Ice branch. Structural aliases remain distinct rows.
* Downward slope entry0xe81d99: first decrements z, checks usability and the
  tile BELOW, then direct/compressed sub-switches choose Grassy/Dry/Dead
  plant adjective, material, Glacial, construction and15 connections of
  Downward Track with natural/construction/Ice sources. Unsupported below-
  tile routes emit plain Downward Slope. All selectors/defaults retained.
* Open Space entry0xe82dcd. Default entry0xe82de1 emits Unknown.

Wall-family order and qualities
At0xe82df3: optional Warm, Damp, Muddy, Snow-covered, Mossy; then optional
Detailed/Sculpted with quality marks or Smooth/Straight/Exposed/Rough-hewn;
then construction descriptor, Ice or material noun; then one of Wall,
Cluster, Fortification, Pillar. Shape and material selection sub-switches
retain aliases and their fallback edges. Warm/Damp are specific to this
earlier wall route; plants leave through0xe834d4 and do not acquire them.
Quality0 uses no marks;1'-',2'+',3'*',4byte0xf0(≡),5byte0x0f(☼).
Other quality values reach the unmarked form. Marks are inline byte writes,
not string literals. Floor chooses Detailed, wall chooses Detailed/Sculpted
from its branch; the mark surrounds that word before its trailing space.

Material, construction and plant dynamic input boundaries
---------------------------------------------------------
0x14d0c70 material-decode resolves coordinates/tile/block geology,
construction/material overrides and state into type/index/state output
fields. Its225-selector compressed table and7-selector direct table,
including default destinations, are in native-switches.tsv; it emits no
caption literals itself.0x14add70 resolves type/index to material pointers;
missing/invalid inputs return null to the text formatter.

0x14d1920 material-noun resets its output, optionally emits material owner's
generated name+"'s ", optional material.prefix(+0x520)+space, and state text.
State-name lives material+0xb8+state*0x20; adjective form uses+0x178 instead.
Natural terrain requests the noun; construction reads the adjective state0.
Null material ->"unknown material" and false return. Special no-index flags
choose plant, yarn, cloth, silk, bone, leather, shell, soap, ivory/tooth, horn,
pearl, or wood/wooden. These are genuine finite fallback alternatives; RAW
state names such as peat are dynamic strings, not PE string literals.

The material+" Cavern Floor" production follows0xe7f7d8: decode call0xe7f818, noun call
0xe7f843, optional bit15 suffix at0xe7f877. Wet follows0xe7f883 with noun
call0xe7f8fd and suffix0xe7f92b. There is no peat-specific native branch.

0xa46f20 construction descriptor looks up the construction at coordinates.
No construction ->append nothing. Item type4 prefixes "rough ". Reinforced
flag inserts optionally different reinforcing-material adjective+"-", then
"Reinforced ". Base and reinforcing materials independently allow generated
owner+"'s ", RAW prefix and state adjective, or unknown material. Item
type2/4 appends " block", type5 " log", others no suffix. The completed
temporary descriptor passes text normalization0x52d3c0 and appends once.
Shoddy is emitted by caller tile branches, not by this helper.

0x14d1330 is a GRASS EVENT LOOKUP, not a material-adjective formatter.
It returns block_square_event_grassst(event kind4) only for positive amount
at x/y within the block. Terrain reads event+0x8 to lookup plant RAW via
0x14d850; grass plural NAME at RAW+0x50 or grassy stair/slope adjective at
RAW+0x90 supplies text. Sparse<=33, Dense>=67, middle density omits prefix.
The legacy title-sources helper row is corrected to these plant domains.

0x13ffd20 plant-parts reads material plant index and tile type. Its220-
selector remap distinguishes roots,trunk,thick branches,branches,smooth
branches,twigs,cap. RAW-specific names+0x670/0x690/0x6b0/0x6d0/0x6f0/0x710
override the default plural NAME(+0x50)+part suffix when nonempty. Smooth
prefix precedes the branches override as well. Non-tree plant kinds use
NAME+0x70 and capitalization; special tree tiles use plural NAME directly.
Invalid index, absent/empty plant or unsupported material kind adds no text;
unmapped tree tile type takes the helper's empty/cleanup edge. Parent tree/
sapling/shrub branches have their own explicit generic fallback strings.

Generated plant name prefixes precede the growth flag gate. Growth=false
does not remove that name. Growth=true may append repeated ", "+growth plural
RAW name(+0x40), subject to selected plant/tile/part, growth time range,
location and world growth-state gates. Absent/inactive/filtered growth adds
no entry. Repetition is dynamic; no finite number of full list sentences is
claimed. Adventure HUD and cached lookinfo terrain pass true; engraving
sheet title calls pass false. Full gate bodies remain in terrain.asm.

Cached lookinfo constructor and producer
-----------------------------------------
0x406860..0x4084de clears display_str(+0x28), selects16-way table0x4084e0.
Classic0x404420..0x40609e with table0x4060a0.
Types0..12 use the same semantic fields as above, but independent native
assembly: terrain call0x406995 growth=true; item/unit/building typed helpers;
vermin quantity;14 flow selectors; Campfire/Fire; surface-deposit extent;
water/magma complete bracket strings; spoor complete-source shortening.
Notable constructor-specific edges: building-item adds leading space;
spoor uninformed/default state can emit just Track/Spoor; vapor lowercase;
solid extent1 constructor omits quantity prefix while HUD emits thin layer.
Missing typed objects can leave the cleared caption empty and still set
color. Unknown top-level type jumps cleanup leaving empty caption.

Additional type13 Sound uses9-way table0x408520: movement/combat/vocalization/
grinding vary Quiet/Loud or Light/Heavy by size<10; Storytelling, Poem
recitation, Musical voice, Dancing, Preaching. Append " (heard"+[" recently"
if timer>=75]+")"; out-of-range
sound type still appends the heard suffix to the otherwise empty field.
Type14 MemoryMap table0x408544: Creature,Object,Structure,Wall,Upward stair,
Downward stair,Updown stair,Upward ramp,Downward ramp,Floor,Open air, each
" (remembered)"; out-of-range leaves empty. Type15 ExtraSense emits
"Blood of the living (sensed)" and uses the supplied sense color fields.

0x4085f0..0x40a1db producer constructs lookinfost records from coordinates,
visibility/memory/sense flags, map objects, liquid depth, flows, campfires,
fire, surface-deposits and spoor. It calls the constructor before appending
records to the look list; all direct calls/conditional branches and its14-
way flow selector0x40a1dc are retained. Classic start0x4061b0/end0x407d9b.
This record source does not eliminate the independent HUD reformatter.

Other text in the same renderer
--------------------------------
Paging hint0x7f3f21 SIMD-loads complete " to view other pages", with tail
"ages" at0x7f3f2b; final addst0x7f3f46. MOVABS at0x7f5d36 writes Hotkey:.
The complete renderer body also retains compass prose and detailed spoor
sentences after0x7f53ad. Their source operands/calls/conditional branches
are included, as are compass16-way direction table0x7f6ba0 and detailed-
spoor mask/remap0x7f6be0/0x7f6c04. They are adjacent renderer text domains,
not terrain compositor productions; existing compass/spoor grammars handle
their dynamic region/name/body-part/material fields.

Extraction coverage counts (source inventory, not runtime tests)
----------------------------------------------------------------
Primary producer corpus per edition:12 code bodies;34 actual indirect switch tables;4492 route rows
(4461 numeric selector encodings +31 out-of-range guards), including63
mask-unreachable encodings explicitly marked0. Terrain alone has20 tables.
Main terrain table:694 selectors,145 destinations;697 structural enum rows
with native effective entry, including147 early-wall routes and tile0/695/
696 explicit main-table defaults. Across both editions:24 bodies,8984 switch
rows,1394 enum routes,1212 RIP literal references,2 printable inline MOVABS
references,2870 direct CALL rows,3812 branch rows,82 confirmed consumer call
contexts(17terrain+22constructor+2producer per edition),58 selected-look/
paging draw call rows. Repeated operands are counted as references, not as
different output sentences. No game was launched or controlled, and no
in-game final appearance was observed by this source extraction.

The Fortress consumer supplement separately adds240 actual vector-field RIP
references,22 complete owner intervals(including8 leaves),4 Fortress virtual
input/render-wrapper bodies and6 independent draw-helper bodies. Its34 RTTI
ownership rows retain22 actual slots and12 explicit no-direct-slot entries.
It also retains34 actual dedicated-vector-leaf CALL rows and their complete
instruction contexts; all belong to the three known list-owner families.
Vector-owner interval ASM includes the complete unwind span; embedded table
bytes at its end are not counted as newly decompiled instruction branches.
